jobs_results.description:
Global Risk Analyst 
 Location: Lisle, IL, with flexibility to work from our Chicago office

   This position follows a hybrid office schedule, with 3 days per week in Chicago and 2 days per week in Lisle.


  Your Job


 As a Global Risk Analyst, you will apply financial analysis and risk assessment to evaluate customer creditworthiness, quantify risk exposure, and support business decisions that create long-term value. You will own a portfolio of customer accounts, providing insights and recommendations that help balance growth opportunities with prudent risk management. Working closely with commercial teams, you will monitor risk trends, communicate key findings, and identify opportunities to improve processes and decision quality.


  Our Team


 The Global Risk Optimization team partners with businesses around the world to identify financial risks, challenge assumptions, and improve decision quality. We leverage Molex's Risk Philosophy and economic thinking to help the business create long-term value while managing risk effectively. Our team values intellectual curiosity, initiative, collaboration, and accountability, and works closely with stakeholders across functions and geographies to deliver meaningful business impact.


  What You Will Do


 


 
  In alignment with Molex's risk philosophy, completing financial analyses and reviews for the purpose of understanding counterparty risk, determining appropriate credit limits and terms for new and existing customers
  Active portfolio ownership of assigned customer base to monitor and maintain credit risk exposures
  Collaborating and d eveloping partnerships with commercial teams by providing actionable input and recommendations for business risk decisions
  Providing commercial teams with transparency to portfolio performance and risks to help drive profitable decisions
  Continuously seeking opportunities through innovation for process improvement and system optimization
  Advance our Principle-Based Management® culture by applying and reinforcing the company's Core Values and Principles
 
 Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)


 


 
  Bachelor's degree or higher in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Statistics or Business or related field
  Strong experience with Excel (spreadsheet creation/editing, pivot tables, data manipulation/analysis and formula creation) Word and PowerPoint
  Strong communication skills (both written and verbal) necessary for professional interactions with both external and internal contacts
  Ability to proactively engage in a rapidly changing business environment while demonstrating a high level of transparency, accountability, and collaboration
  Detail-oriented and self-motivated with ability to define problems, multi-task, meet deadlines, and be a collaborative team player
 
 


 What Will Put You Ahead


 


 
  One or more years of relevant experience (i.e. financial statement analysis, risk analysis, economic modelling and research, portfolio management, credit, treasury)
  Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Alteryx or other data visualization software/tools
  Proficient with SAP
  Process Transformation / Process Automation / Process Implementation experience
  Language skills in addition to English
 
 For this role, we anticipate paying $75,000 - $80,000 per year. This role is eligible for variable pay, issued as a monetary bonus or in another form.


 At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate's knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. If you have questions, please speak to your recruiter about the flexibility and detail of our compensation philosophy.


  Hiring Philosophy


 All Koch companies value diversity of thought, perspectives, aptitudes, experiences, and backgrounds. We are Military Ready and Second Chance employers. Learn more about our hiring philosophy here .


  Who We Are


 As a Koch company, Molex is a leading supplier of connectors and interconnect components, driving innovation in electronics and supporting industries from automotive to health care and consumer to data communications. The thousands of innovators who work for Molex have made us a global electronics leader. Our experienced people, groundbreaking products and leading-edge technologies help us deliver a wider array of solutions to more markets than ever before.


 At Koch, employees are empowered to do what they do best to make life better. Learn how our business philosophy helps employees unleash their potential while creating value for themselves and the company.


  Our Benefits


 Our goal is for each employee, and their families, to live fulfilling and healthy lives. We provide essential resources and support to build and maintain physical, financial, and emotional strength - focusing on overall wellbeing so you can focus on what matters most. Our benefits plan includes - medical, dental, vision, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, ADD, disability, retirement, paid vacation/time off, educational assistance, and may also include infertility assistance, paid parental leave and adoption assistance. Specific eligibility criteria is set by the applicable Summary Plan Description, policy or guideline and benefits may vary by geographic region. If you have questions on what benefits apply to you, please speak to your recruiter.


 Additionally, everyone has individual work and personal needs. We seek to enable the best work environment that helps you and the business work together to produce superior results.


  Equal Opportunities 


 Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status. Except where prohibited by state law, some offers of employment are conditioned upon successfully passing a drug test. jobs_results.title: Analyst, Risk & Insurance

job_highlights.title: Qualifications
items: EXPERIENCE: Three (3) years' of experience in data heavy administrative support, claims/benefits operations, analytics support, or related fields with strong Excel proficiency
EDUCATION AND TRAINING: High School degree required
CERTIFICATES, LICENSES & REGISTRATIONS: None

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Knowledge of claims administration processes, risk management practices, and the use of risk management information systems (RMIS) within a public sector or educational environment, including general familiarity with workers' compensation, liability, and incident reporting requirements

Knowledge of data governance principles, record retention standards, and public records requirements, including the Colorado Open Records Act (CORA) and data privacy expectations applicable to school districts
Knowledge of basic analytical concepts, reporting methodologies, and common metrics used to evaluate claims activity, losses, and risk trends
Skilled in maintaining structured electronic records, applying consistent naming conventions, metadata standards, and access controls to support audit readiness, legal discovery, and records requests

Ability to analyze claims and incident data to identify patterns, trends, and potential risk indicators and to communicate findings clearly to the Claims Manager, Director of Risk Management, and other stakeholders

Ability to manage multiple reporting cycles, respond to ad hoc data requests, and support time sensitive activities such as high risk activity reviews, travel tracking, and records requests while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality, and attention to detail

The physical requirements, mental requirements and work environment factors described below are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions
PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Ability to focus on objects at varying distances and distinguish between colors (with corrective lenses)
Perform tasks that require manual dexterity, including operation of computers & small office equipment
Basic mobility and the ability to navigate the office environment safely
Ability to speak clearly, listen attentively (with assistance devices), and convey information accurately
May be required to give presentations to groups
MENTAL FUNCTIONS: Ability to analyze situations, identify potential risks, and devise effective solutions
Ability to remain flexible in dynamic environments, adjusting plans and strategies as necessary to accommodate changing requirements or circumstances
Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate with other teams
Ability to manage time and priorities to meet deadlines
WORK ENVIRONMENT: Work is performed in a semi-secured office building with a typical office environment and risk factors

items: SUMMARY Supports claims operations by maintaining and organizing accurate claims data in collaboration with the Claims Manager and Director of Risk Management
Creates routine and ad hoc reports, dashboards, and summaries to support reporting and decision-making
Reviews data for accuracy and completeness, resolving errors and inconsistencies as needed
Tracks claims activity trends and processes high-risk activity and travel requests following established procedures
Maintains organized records to support audits, legal requests, and public records requirements
Helps ensure timely, accurate information is available to support effective claims management across the District
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions

Collaborate with Claims Manager and Director of Risk Management to refine reporting specifications, define required data fields within the risk management information system (RMIS), and improve the consistency and functionality of claims data and reporting tools
Standardize incoming data (incident reports, medical invoices, internal logs) by applying naming conventions, data validation rules, and controlled vocabularies to support accurate reporting

Create analysis-ready datasets by transforming raw RMIS extracts (e.g. Excel files) using established data-cleaning routines, field mapping, normalization, controlled vocabulary alignment, and key-field matching
Assist in organizing, sorting, filtering, and coding claims data to support operational reporting needs
Perform routine data audits to identify missing information, duplicate records, or data inconsistencies

Track and monitor trends in incident types, common injuries, and reporting patterns using established spreadsheets and district templates
Prepare data reports and visualizations (charts, graphs, tables) that clearly communicate trends and respond to leadership requests regarding claims activity and losses in the district
Review and process high-risk activity (HRA) and travel requests in a timely manner in accordance with established procedures
Maintain shared tracking tools, document follow-up actions and materials received and prepare summary information for Claims Manager and Director of Risk Management and cross-functional partners
Maintain retention-ready electronic records by applying consistent file structures, metadata standards, and appropriate access controls within shared repositories

Assemble data packets and structured exports to support audits, legal discovery, and Colorado Open Records Act (CORA) responses under the direction of the Claims Manager and Director of Risk Management, ensuring completeness and data privacy compliance
Perform other duties as assigned

Skilled in organizing, cleaning, standardizing, and validating data from multiple sources such as incident reports, medical invoices, internal logs, and RMIS extracts to produce analysis ready datasets

Skilled in using spreadsheet and reporting tools (e.g., Excel) to sort, filter, code, analyze, and visualize claims data, including the preparation of charts, tables, and summary reports for operational and leadership audiences

jobs_results.description:
About the role




The Onboarding & Risk Analyst is a full-time hybrid salary position + full health benefits, unlimited PTO, & 401k. 




The ORA decides which businesses can move money on Straddle. You will review new merchant and platform applications, determine whether each one fits our risk appetite and sponsor bank requirements, and document your decision so it holds up in an audit. You will work closely with our Risk Lead and Head of Compliance and escalate to them as needed.




Day to day, you will work the onboarding queue. That means running KYB and KYC CDD reviews, verifying business entities and beneficial owners, screening for sanctions and adverse media, and checking each applicant's business model, flow of funds, and website against what they told us.




We are preparing for a major go-to-market push and expect application volume to rise sharply. Your job is to help us approve good businesses quickly and keep the wrong ones off, without lowering our standards. You will also help refine our review criteria, risk tiers, and SOPs as volume grows.




We're looking for strong analytical and communication skills, sound judgment, and a working knowledge of KYB/KYC and BSA/AML, or the drive to learn them quickly.



What you'll do





 Onboarding Reviews - Review new merchant and platform applications end to end. Verify business entities, beneficial ownership, and principals, and confirm each applicant has cleared the required KYB/KYC checks before going live.
 Risk Assessment & Classification - Evaluate each applicant's business model, industry, MCC, and flow of funds to assign the right risk tier. Identify when a business needs licensing, such as money transmission, lending, or earned wage access, and when a business falls outside our risk appetite.
 Enhanced Due Diligence - Run EDD on higher-risk applicants. Review terms of service, privacy policies, marketing, and entity documents against what the applicant told us, and flag any inconsistencies. Draft clear, specific follow-up requests to applicants and partners.
 Sanctions, Watchlist & Adverse Media Screening - Review screening results for businesses and their principals. Resolve false positives with documented rationale, and escalate true matches promptly and in full.
 Decisioning & Documentation - Make and document approve, conditional-approve, and decline recommendations. Write each decision so a sponsor bank, auditor, or examiner can follow your reasoning without asking you a question.
 Limits & Ongoing Monitoring - Recommend initial transaction limits based on expected volume and risk profile. Support periodic re-reviews of existing merchants when their activity, return rates, or business model changes.
 Queue Management & SLAs - Own the onboarding pipeline during a high-volume launch period. Prioritize well, keep applications from stalling, and communicate status clearly to Sales, Customer Success, and applicants.
 Onboarding & Risk Support - Support the Risk Lead and the broader compliance team across onboarding and risk work. Answer applicant and partner questions about requirements, help with escalated or complex cases, and take on ad hoc risk reviews and projects as priorities shift.
 Process & Policy Improvement - Help refine onboarding SOPs, risk-tiering criteria, and review checklists as volume grows. Spot repeat patterns and suggest ways to automate or streamline reviews without lowering the bar.
 Bank Partner & Audit Support - Prepare due diligence packages and evidence for sponsor bank reviews, audits, and exams, as directed by the Risk Lead and Head of Compliance.


Qualifications



Required Qualifications





 Professional Experience - 1 to 3 years of experience in KYB/KYC onboarding, merchant underwriting, risk operations, compliance, or payment operations. Ideally at a fintech, bank, or payments company where the work had real regulatory stakes.
 Analytical Judgment - You can read a business's website, documents, and application and tell whether the story holds together. You catch mismatches between what a business says it does and what it actually does, and you ask when something doesn't add up.
 Written Communication - You write concise, well-supported risk decisions and clear requests for information. Your documentation stands on its own.
 Comfort with Volume - You work methodically through a busy queue without cutting corners. You know which applications need a fast yes and which need a closer look.
 Startup Readiness - You are comfortable with ambiguity in a small, fast-moving company. You can hold multiple workstreams at once, make calls with incomplete information, and know when to escalate.
 Integrity and Discretion - You bring high integrity and sound judgment to sensitive information. You will see personal identifying information, business financials, and compliance case files daily. Confidentiality and professional conduct are non-negotiable.


Preferred Qualifications





 High-Risk Industry Experience - Experience underwriting or reviewing higher-risk verticals such as lending, earned wage access, marketplaces, P2P, or regulated goods.
 Payments and Regulatory Exposure - Familiarity with ACH, Nacha Operating Rules, BSA/AML, CIP and beneficial ownership requirements, OFAC, and state money transmission licensing.
 Sponsor Bank Experience - Experience working within bank-partner programs and their due diligence requirements.
 Certification Interest - Interest in or progress toward CAMS, CAFS, CAFCA, or similar industry certifications. We support continuing education.
 Tool Familiarity - Experience with Plain, Linear, Notion, or Salesforce is helpful but not required.
 AI-Augmented Work - Experience using AI tools to improve review quality or throughput. We are a technology company and expect our team to use the best tools available.




About Straddle


Straddle is building the trust layer for how money moves in the United States. The payments infrastructure behind $100 trillion in annual volume was designed for batch processing and banking hours. We're rebuilding it for businesses that need money to move fast and land with confidence.




Straddle is an open-banking payments platform for account-to-account money movement. One API combines identity verification, fraud detection, and payments across ACH and RTP, with FedNow coming soon, so businesses can move money between bank accounts as easily as sending a text.




The pay range for this role is:




70,000 - 88,000 USD per year (Broomfield Office)
